The PKGBUILD file is a standard Arch Linux package build script for the "keeplog" package. During sourcing (as performed by makepkg --printsrcinfo), only top-level variable assignments and the source array are evaluated—none of which execute any external commands or perform network operations. There are no command substitutions, eval calls, curl/wget invocations, or any other potentially dangerous constructs at the global scope. All potentially side-effecting logic resides within the build() and package() functions, which are not executed during makepkg --printsrcinfo. The source array points to the project's official GitHub repository (https://github.com/rathinadev/keeplog) using a version-tagged archive, which is consistent with standard packaging practices and does not raise security concerns for this specific command's execution.

This is a standard .gitignore file for an AUR package. It uses the common pattern of ignoring all files (*) while explicitly allowing only the packaging-related files: .nvchecker.toml (version checking config), .gitignore itself, PKGBUILD (the build script), and .SRCINFO (package metadata). This is a normal and expected practice in AUR repositories to keep the git history clean by tracking only the packaging files, not build artifacts or upstream source code. There are no network requests, code execution, obfuscation, or any suspicious behavior.
